life_expectancy.label: Life Expectancy at Birth
life_expectancy.description: Average number of years a newborn is expected to live, based on current mortality rates across all age groups in Singapore.
life_expectancy.source: Department of Statistics Singapore (SingStat), Table M810501
life_expectancy.tooltip: Based on period life tables published by SingStat. Reflects the average lifespan if current-year mortality rates persist. Not a prediction for any individual. The dip in 2021–2022 reflects excess COVID-19 mortality.

diabetes_prevalence.label: Diabetes Prevalence
diabetes_prevalence.description: Percentage of Singapore residents aged 18–74 diagnosed with or found to have diabetes mellitus.
diabetes_prevalence.source: MOH National Population Health Survey (NPHS) via SingStat Table M870401
diabetes_prevalence.tooltip: Measured via fasting blood glucose or HbA1c during health surveys. Includes both previously diagnosed and newly detected cases. Survey age range changed from 18–69 to 18–74 in 2017. Comparisons across years should note methodology changes.

hypertension_prevalence.label: Hypertension Prevalence
hypertension_prevalence.description: Percentage of Singapore residents aged 18–74 with high blood pressure (systolic ≥ 140 mmHg or diastolic ≥ 90 mmHg, or on medication).
hypertension_prevalence.source: MOH NPHS via SingStat Table M870401
hypertension_prevalence.tooltip: From 2020, NPHS adopted a new methodology using the average of multiple blood pressure readings and expanded the age range to 18–74. This caused reported prevalence to jump from 24.2% (2017) to 35.5% (2020). The increase is largely methodological, not a real surge in hypertension.

obesity_prevalence.label: Obesity Prevalence
obesity_prevalence.description: Percentage of Singapore residents aged 18–74 with BMI ≥ 30 kg/m².
obesity_prevalence.source: MOH NPHS via SingStat Table M870401
obesity_prevalence.tooltip: Based on measured BMI (weight/height²) during health surveys. Uses WHO obesity threshold of BMI ≥ 30. Asian populations may have higher metabolic risk at lower BMI — Singapore also tracks 'overweight' at BMI ≥ 25.

high_cholesterol_prevalence.label: Hyperlipidaemia
high_cholesterol_prevalence.description: Percentage of Singapore residents aged 18–74 with high total cholesterol (≥ 6.2 mmol/L) or on lipid-lowering medication.
high_cholesterol_prevalence.source: MOH NPHS via SingStat Table M870401
high_cholesterol_prevalence.tooltip: Measured via fasting blood lipid panel during health surveys. Includes those on lipid-lowering medication. The drop in 2022 may reflect increased medication use and better management rather than less hyperlipidaemia.

daily_smoking_rate.label: Daily Smoking Rate
daily_smoking_rate.description: Percentage of Singapore residents aged 18–74 who smoke daily.
daily_smoking_rate.source: MOH NPHS via SingStat Table M870401
daily_smoking_rate.tooltip: Self-reported daily smoking status during health surveys. The consistent decline reflects decades of tobacco control policy including plain packaging, high excise taxes, and progressively raised minimum legal age.

govt_health_expenditure.label: Government Health Expenditure
govt_health_expenditure.description: Total Singapore government expenditure on health (operating + development), in billions of Singapore dollars.
govt_health_expenditure.tooltip: Includes operating expenditure (hospitals, polyclinics, subsidies) and development expenditure (new facilities, infrastructure). The sharp increase from 2019 to 2021 was driven by COVID-19 pandemic response. These are nominal figures (not inflation-adjusted). Per capita spend was S$2,976 in 2022.

chronic_disease_screening.label: Chronic Disease Screening Rate
chronic_disease_screening.description: Percentage of Singapore residents who were screened for chronic diseases at the recommended frequency.
chronic_disease_screening.source: MOH NPHS via SingStat Table M870401
chronic_disease_screening.tooltip: Covers screening for diabetes, hypertension, and hyperlipidaemia per MOH recommended intervals. The Screen for Life programme subsidises these screenings at CHAS GP clinics and polyclinics.

binge_drinking.label: Binge Drinking
binge_drinking.description: Percentage of Singapore residents who engaged in binge drinking (5+ drinks on a single occasion for men, 4+ for women) in the past month.
binge_drinking.source: MOH NPHS via SingStat Table M870401
binge_drinking.tooltip: Self-reported binge drinking. The steady increase over time reflects changing social drinking patterns. Binge drinking is a risk factor for liver disease, injuries, and cardiovascular events.

physical_activity.label: Sufficient Physical Activity
physical_activity.description: Percentage of Singapore residents meeting WHO-recommended levels of physical activity (≥150 min moderate or ≥75 min vigorous per week).
physical_activity.source: MOH NPHS via SingStat Table M870401
physical_activity.tooltip: Self-reported via the Global Physical Activity Questionnaire (GPAQ). 'Sufficient' means meeting WHO minimum of 150 minutes moderate or 75 minutes vigorous activity per week. The post-2019 decline may partly reflect COVID-19 restrictions.

childhood_obesity.label: Childhood Obesity (Pri 1)
childhood_obesity.description: Prevalence of overweight and severely overweight (obesity) among Primary 1 children in Singapore.
childhood_obesity.tooltip: Measured during the annual School Health Service screening of Primary 1 students (age ~7). Combines overweight and severely overweight categories. The spike in 2021 (13.4%) likely reflects reduced physical activity during COVID-19 school closures.

health_personnel.label: Doctors per 10,000
health_personnel.description: Number of registered doctors per 10,000 total population in Singapore.
health_personnel.tooltip: Includes all registered medical practitioners (GPs, specialists, house officers). The gradual increase reflects Singapore's efforts to expand healthcare workforce capacity to meet growing demand from an aging population.

hospital_beds.label: Hospital Beds (Acute)
hospital_beds.description: Total number of beds in acute hospitals (public and private) in Singapore.
hospital_beds.tooltip: Includes public, not-for-profit, and private acute hospital beds. Does not include community hospital or psychiatric hospital beds. The gradual increase reflects infrastructure expansion to serve a growing and aging population.

cancer_incidence.label: Cancer Incidence
cancer_incidence.description: Age-standardised incidence rate of all cancers per 100,000 population. Based on 5-year period averages from the Singapore Cancer Registry.
cancer_incidence.tooltip: Cancer incidence has risen steadily, driven partly by aging population and better detection. Despite rising diagnoses, survival rates have improved significantly. 1 in 4 Singaporeans will develop cancer in their lifetime.

cancer_mortality.label: Cancer Mortality
cancer_mortality.description: Age-standardised mortality rate from all cancers per 100,000 population. Based on 5-year period averages from the Singapore Cancer Registry.
cancer_mortality.tooltip: Despite rising cancer incidence, mortality rates have declined steadily since the 1980s — reflecting advances in early detection, treatment, and screening programmes like Screen for Life.

deaths_by_cause.label: Deaths by Cause
deaths_by_cause.description: Annual deaths in Singapore broken down by major cause, showing the epidemiological transition from infectious diseases to chronic non-communicable diseases over five decades.
deaths_by_cause.source: Registry of Births and Deaths, SingStat Table M810131
deaths_by_cause.tooltip: Shows how Singapore's mortality profile shifted dramatically since 1969. Cancer, heart disease, and pneumonia now dominate, while infectious diseases have been nearly eliminated. "Other Causes" combines kidney disease, digestive system diseases, accidents and suicides, diabetes, nervous system diseases (including dementia), and remaining conditions.

psychiatric_admissions.label: Psychiatric Admissions
psychiatric_admissions.description: Annual admissions to psychiatric hospitals in Singapore.
psychiatric_admissions.tooltip: Tracks public psychiatric hospital admissions (primarily Institute of Mental Health). The steady increase from 2021 onward may reflect growing mental health needs and reduced stigma around seeking help. Does not capture outpatient psychiatric visits.

tb_incidence.label: Tuberculosis Incidence
tb_incidence.description: Incidence rate of tuberculosis per 100,000 population in Singapore.
tb_incidence.tooltip: Singapore still has an intermediate TB burden compared to other developed countries. The decline from 2022 onward may reflect improved screening and treatment. TB remains a notifiable disease in Singapore.

aged_65_plus.label: Population Aged 65+
aged_65_plus.description: Percentage of Singapore resident population aged 65 years and over.
aged_65_plus.source: Department of Statistics Singapore (SingStat), Table M810011
aged_65_plus.tooltip: Singapore is one of the fastest-aging societies in Asia. The proportion aged 65+ has more than doubled since 2000, driven by longer life expectancy and low fertility rates. By 2030, roughly 1 in 4 residents will be 65+.

old_age_support_ratio.label: Old-Age Support Ratio
old_age_support_ratio.description: Number of residents aged 20-64 per resident aged 65 and over. A lower ratio means fewer working-age adults supporting each elderly person.
old_age_support_ratio.source: Department of Statistics Singapore (SingStat), Table M810001
old_age_support_ratio.tooltip: The old-age support ratio measures how many working-age adults (20-64) support each elderly person (65+). A declining ratio signals increasing fiscal pressure on healthcare, pensions, and social services. Singapore's ratio has fallen sharply from 8.4 in 2005 to around 3.6 in 2024.

total_fertility_rate.label: Total Fertility Rate
total_fertility_rate.description: Average number of live births per woman over her lifetime, assuming current age-specific fertility rates persist.
total_fertility_rate.source: Department of Statistics Singapore (SingStat), Table M810091
total_fertility_rate.tooltip: A TFR of 2.1 is needed for population replacement without immigration. Singapore's TFR has been well below replacement level since the 1980s and hit a historic low of 0.87 in 2025 (preliminary) — one of the lowest in the world. This drives the aging population trend.
